paragraphs: Ita bammidrash pelia en mannichin tepillin ella beshabbat, vehu pele veharab mhrsh"m za"l peresh bazeh b"liqqute shoshannim" shello shebbesop seper "qarnayim" yeuyyan sham, ak shamati beshem haggaon rabbi aqiba eger za"l shepperesh bshb"t rashe tebot bimqom sear bimqom tappucha ki tepillin shel rosh dino lehannicho bimqom sear utepillin shel yad tzarik lehannicho bappereq hattachton hassamuk lekattep babbasar haggabohha vehattappucha hanniqra qibboret leshon "qibbure daahine" deperusho qebutzat hattemarim, veken rotzeh lomar qebutzat habbasar vehaynu basar hattopeach. al ken tzarik lehazhir et haam bazeh, biprat bitpillin shel rosh yesh harbeh nikshalim veen medaqdeqim bekak, utzerikin lehizzaher shettehe haqqatzeh hattachton shel hattittura munnach al meqom hatchalat iqqere hassear sheggam hattittura hi mikkelal hattepillin, veadam sheyyesh lo searot arukkot veshokebot ad chatzi hammetzach ap al pi shemmannicha hattepillin al hassear la mehanne debaenan mehatchalat iqqere hassear ulemala, veshiur maqom zeh hu ad shemmocho shel hattinoq ropes, veim hinnicho lematta bemaqom shekkalu iqqere hassear hare zeh midderek haqqaraim velo qiyyem hammitzva vegam neenash al kak, umihu ish zaqen shennasheru searot rosho veken haqqerach ap al pi sheen lahem atta sear rosham yannichu hattepillin bemaqom shehaya bo miqqodem sear vezeh nikkar bechush hareut sheyyesh hepresh ben or haqqarecha laor sheen tzomeach sham sear etzel kol adam veda ki besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" hebeti dibre harab "chayye adam" shekkatab im rubbo shel bayit munnach bimqom sear veraq miuto al hammetzach bemaqom shekkalu iqqere hassearot lo yatza yede chobato debaenan kullo mammash bimqom sear, vehebeti dibre harab "nachal eshkol" beseper "haeshkol" sop hilkot tepillin shehebi dibre harab "chayye adam" hannizkar veheela ken, gam zakarti sham mah shekkatabti besiyyata dishmayya besipre haq' "rab berakot" dap qp"z bedin happarashiyyot hayyotzeot chutz labbayit, upilpalti bidbarim ellu vesop dabar heeleti kisbarat harab "chayye adam" za"l debaenan kol habbayit kullo bimqom shaar:

clarification.explanation: The midrash states, puzzlingly, that tefillin are worn only on "Shabbat" — seemingly a wonder, since one certainly wears tefillin on the other days of the week too! Some explain that "Shabbat" here is an acronym: "se'ar" (hair) and "tapuach" (swelling) — the head-tefillin must be placed on the place of the hair, and the hand-tefillin must be placed on the raised, swelling flesh (called the "kiboret") on the lower part of the arm near the shoulder. One must caution the public, especially regarding the head-tefillin, since many are not careful enough: the lower edge of the "titura" (the base of the box) must rest exactly at the start of the hair roots. Someone with long hair reaching down to the middle of the forehead is still obligated to place the tefillin at the true start of the hair roots (not wherever appears to be covered by hair due to its length), because the place is measured up to the point where an infant's skull is still soft. If he placed it lower than that, this is the way of the Karaites and he has not fulfilled the mitzvah, and is even punished for it. An elderly man whose hair has fallen out, or a bald man, still places the tefillin at the place where the hair originally was, which can be distinguished by sight from skin that naturally never grows hair at all. Rabbi Yosef Chaim also rules that the entire box of the tefillin (not merely most of it) must rest exactly at the place of the hair, and it is not sufficient for most of it to be on the place of hair with only a small part on the forehead.
takeaways: The head-tefillin must rest exactly at the start of the hair roots (up to the point of the infant's soft skull), not lower, even if the hair is long.
The entire box of the tefillin (not merely most of it) must rest on the place of the hair — this is a strict ruling many are not careful about.

paragraphs: Gam haqqesher shel harosh yihyeh munnach bimqom sear, begobah haorep shehu sop etzem haggulgolet vehu keneged happanim, veim mannicha haqqesher al hatztzavvar lo asa kelum sheen zeh niqra orep:

clarification.explanation: The knot of the strap of the head-tefillin must also rest at a place that has hair — at the height of the nape of the neck, which is the end of the skull bone (the point opposite the face). If one places the knot on the neck (below the true nape), he has not fulfilled the mitzvah at all.
takeaways: The knot of the head-tefillin must be at the height of the nape (on a place of hair), not on the neck.

paragraphs: Tzarik lekavven hattepillin shel rosh shettehe haqqetzitza beemtza rochab harosh kede shettehe ben haenayim, veken tzarik sheyyehe haqqesher gam ken beemtza haorep lo yatteh lekan o lekan, gam hammaqom shebbeqesher shennireh keen dale"t yihyeh letzad chutz, velo kelappe haorep, vehu haddin beqesher tepillin shel yad yizzaher shello yithappek, veim nithappek nakon lehitannot, veim qasheh alayv hattaanit yipdehu bitzdaqa:

clarification.explanation: One must position the head-tefillin so that the box (the kitzitza) sits exactly at the center of the width of the head, between the eyes. Likewise, the knot must be exactly at the center of the nape, not tilted to one side. The shape resembling the letter dalet formed by the strap around the knot must face outward, not toward the nape. The same law applies to the knot of the hand-tefillin — one must be careful that it does not turn over; and if it did turn over, it is proper to fast (and if the fast is too difficult, one may redeem it with charity).
takeaways: Exact placement: the box of the head-tefillin between the eyes, the knot at the center of the nape with the "dalet" shape facing outward.
If the knot of the hand-tefillin turns over, it is proper to fast a day, or to redeem the fast with charity.

paragraphs: Habbattim veharetzuot tepillin shel rosh utepillin shel yad tzarik sheyyihyu shechorot halaka lemosheh missinay, velaken im nitlabbenu mechamat yeshnan tzarik lehashchiram, veim hishchiram goy pesulim, vetzarik sheyyihyeh tzad hashshachor shebbaretzuot letzad chutz veim nithappeka haretzua shessebib harosh, veken haretzua sheqqosher bah haqqetzitza, yitanneh yom echad veha derab huna hitanna baabur zeh arbaim yom zo middat chasidut yetera havet beh, vetob lizzaher gam birtzuot tepillin shel rosh hamshulshalot ad hechazeh vehattabbur, veken retzua shel tepillin shel yad shekkorek al hazzeroa shello yithappeku, veap al gab deal pi hassod mashchirin haretzuot panim veachor shechorot kaoreb kannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot lerabbenu haari"y za"l, lo nahagnu bekak veshaalti al minhag hachasidim beir haqqodesh tibbaneh vetikkonen bimhera beyamenu veameru li sheyyesh nizharin lehashchir panim veachor, veyesh sheen medaqdeqin bazeh:

clarification.explanation: The boxes and straps of both the head-tefillin and hand-tefillin must be black — this is a halacha given to Moshe at Sinai. If they faded from use, one must blacken them again; but if a non-Jew blackened them, they are invalid. The black side of the straps must face outward. If any strap (the one around the head, or the one with which the box is tied) turned over, one should fast for one day (the fact that Rav Huna fasted forty days over this was his own exceptional measure of piety, not an obligation for everyone). One must also be careful with the long straps hanging down to the chest and navel, and with the strap wound around the arm, that they not turn over. Although according to the Kabbalah there is a method of blackening the straps on both sides (front and back) as taught by the Ari, of blessed memory, that was not the practice where Rabbi Yosef Chaim lived; some of the pious in Jerusalem are indeed careful about this.
takeaways: The boxes and straps of the tefillin must be black, and must be blackened by a Jew (not a non-Jew).
A strap turning over (the non-black side facing outward) requires a day's fast (or redemption with charity).

paragraphs: Lo yihyeh dabar chotzetz ben tepillin libsaro hen babbattim hen birtzuot, veim yesh likluk tzarik lerachatzu, vehallobesh batte enayim yizzaher shello yitchob otam ben haretzua uben besaro, ella yitchabem ben haretzua uben hakkoba, veim i epshar lo belav haki tzarik sheyyizzaher bazeh lepachot biqriat shema ubirkoteha ubitpillat haamida, vehaacharonim za"l piqpequ bimgaddele shaar harbeh berosham dekevan digdelim harbeh lekka lememar haynu rebutayhu ledaat haro"sh za"l, vegam ledaat harashba" za"l hane searot merubbim have ketachboshet makka vechayetzi keshellobesh hattepillin alehem, veken piqpequ bisar harosh hayyored lematta delav meqom rebiteh hu vechotzetz, vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam bidbarim keillu bekol mah deepshar bemitzva rabba viqara zo:

clarification.explanation: Nothing may intervene between the tefillin (whether the boxes or the straps) and the flesh. If there is dirt, it must be washed off. One who wears eyeglasses must be careful not to tuck them between the strap and his flesh, but rather between the strap and his hat; and if this cannot be avoided otherwise, he must at least be careful about it during the reading of the Shema and its blessings and the Amidah prayer. The later authorities discussed the case of someone with very abundant hair on his head — if it is excessively thick, there is concern that it constitutes an interposition between the tefillin and the head (unless this is the ordinary condition for people generally). They likewise discussed hair that hangs down below its place of natural growth, which may also constitute an interposition. One must caution the public about these matters as much as possible, given the great importance of this mitzvah.
takeaways: Nothing (eyeglasses, dirt) may be placed between the tefillin and the flesh, at least during the reading of the Shema and the Amidah prayer.
Overly thick or overly long hair at the place of the tefillin may be considered an interposition and invalidate the mitzvah.

paragraphs: Kebar amarnu leel dehannachat tepillin shel yad bazzeroa bappereq hattachton hassamuk lekattep babbasar haggabohha hanniqra qibboret, velo yannichennu lematta mehaqqibboret debaenan sima keneged halleb vehaqqibboret mekuvvan keneged halleb, velaken tzarik shita hattepillin shel yad letzad haggup meat, beinyan dekaasher yakop hazzeroa lematta yehe hattepillin shel yad mekuvvan keneged libbo mammash, vaapillu bappereq hattachton hannizkar yizzaher shello yannichennu bachatzi haelyon shel happereq hannizkar samuk lebet hashshechi, ap al pi shennimshak sham basar haggabohha, ella yannicho bachetzi hassamuk lappereq haemtzai bimqom basar haggabohha shebbo, uledaat haggaon rabbenu eliyyahu mivvilena za"l kol maqom basar haggabohha kasher gam oto hacheleq hannimshak bachatzi hassamuk lebet hashshechi, veayyen "chayye adam" kelal y"d ot y, ushear acharonim za"l, ubesipri haq' "mqbtzyl" haaleti besiyyata dishmayya dilkattechilla tzarik lachush lisbarat happoseqim disbira lehu bachatzi hashsheni lo yannicha tepillin apillu al basar haggabohha hammaggia sham, velaken hallobesh rashi"y verabbenu tam beyachad yizzaher laasotam qetannim kede sheyyukal lehannicham al basar tappucha shebbachatzi harishon shel happereq, veheka dela epshar behaki yesh lismok al sebarat haggaon rabbi eliyyahu mivvilena za"l hannizkar disbira leh kol basar haqqibboret rauy lehannicha bo tepillin:

clarification.explanation: As mentioned, the hand-tefillin are placed on the lower joint of the arm near the shoulder, on the raised flesh (the "kiboret") — not lower than that, because they must be aligned opposite the heart, and the kiboret is aligned opposite the heart. Therefore one must tilt the tefillin slightly toward the body, so that when the arm is bent downward, the tefillin will be exactly opposite the heart. Even within the lower joint itself, one must not place it in the upper half (near the armpit), but rather in the half near the middle joint, at the raised flesh found there. One opinion (the Gra) is more lenient and validates the entire area of raised flesh, including the part near the armpit. Rabbi Yosef Chaim rules that ideally one should be concerned for the stricter view — therefore one who wears both Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin together should be careful to make them small so they fit in the correct place, and only when there is no other option may one rely on the Gra.
takeaways: Hand-tefillin should be placed on the lower-middle part of the arm (the kiboret), not on the upper part near the armpit, and should be tilted slightly so as to be opposite the heart; therefore one who wears Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam together should make them small so they can be placed there, relying on the Gra's leniency only when there is no other option.

paragraphs: Hannachat tepillin shel yad bismol, shehi yad keha vetash kochah, veitter yad yemino im oseh kol melakto bismolo yannicha tepillin shel yad bismolo shehu yemin kol adam, veim sholet bishte yadayv yannicha bismol kol adam, veim koteb bimino ushear kol maasayv oseh bismolo, o koteb bismol ushear maasayv oseh beyamin, yesh omerim sheyyannicha bayyad shettash kochah debaenan yad keha, veyesh omerim shehayyad shekkoteb bah hi chashiba yamin leinyan zeh, umannicha tepillin bayyad shekkenegdah, mishshum desamak hakkatub "uqeshartam" l"uketabtam" mah ketiba beyamin ap qeshira beyamin, umiddeqashira beyamin mikkelal dehannacha al hassemol, dibyad shehu koteb bah tzarik liqshor hattepillin al yad shekkenegdah vekol zeh katub umeporash bedibre maran za"l siman k"z seip v yeuyyan sham, ak harab "shalme tzibbur" dap m' ammud g katab sheharab hamqubbal mahari"y tzemach za"l beseper "zer zahab" heerik veharbeh birayot deitter yad yemino eno rashshay leshannot mishshear kol adam shello leshannot hasseder haelyon ayyen sham, vehebi debarayv b"pitche teshuba" vegam beseper "meir laaretz" ubeemet dibre harab mahari"y tzemach za"l nekonim bitamim al pi hassod vegabra rabba amar milleta demistabber tameh, al ken haaleti besiata dishmayya besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" dilolam itter yad yaaseh kisbarat maran za"l vekol happoseqim happashtanim disbira lehu im oseh kol melakto bismol yannicha tepillin shel yad bismolo shehu yemin kol adam, veyitpallel bitpillin zeh ak achar hattepilla yilbash tepillin bismol kol adam velo yebarek alehem beshem umalkut ella yeharher shem umalkut belibbo veyiqra q"sh belo berakot vikavven latzet y"ch sebarat mahari"tz za"l, ak zeh tzarik laasot shette tsh"y echad kepi hannachat yad yamin veechad kepi hannachat yad semol d" lehishtammesh beechad lishte yadayim mippene haqqesher shel hayyo"d shello yetze lachutz im yithappek, v"p sheshshaalti al minhag h"q tvb"b v"l sheen minhagam lachush lisbarat mahari"tz za"l hnz', k"z ani omer yr"sh yatza y"ch mitzva zo allibba dk" ki hi mitzva yeqara, umah gam desabera zo mistabber tamah "p hassod, vesham hebeti dibre harab chs"l za"l baopen shekkatab besi' k"z ot Adonai upiqpaqti bidbarayv vehu pashut: beram im zeh katub bimin kol adam, yesh lehorot lo bipshitut sheyyismok bazeh al sebarat haomer shehayyad hakkoteb bah hi chashiba yamin, "p shekkol maasayv oseh beotah shekkenegdah veyannicha tepillin bismol shehu semol kol adam, velah en tzarik lehatricho lehannicha paam shenit kepi sebarat man diplig, mippene ki bikhay gavna shehu koteb bimin kol adam gam happoseqim happashtanim ikka ds"l dimhanne behaki deazelinan batar hakketiba, dehayyad shekkoteb bah chashiba yamin "p shekkol maasayv oseh beotah shekkenegdah, veim gam bazeh yirtzeh lehannicha paam shenit laasot allibba dk" tabo alayv beraka:

clarification.explanation: The hand-tefillin are placed on the left hand (the weaker, "feeble" hand). A left-handed person (whose left hand functions as the dominant hand, the way the right hand functions for most people) who does all his work with his left hand places the hand-tefillin on his left hand (which is functionally the "right" hand for every person). One who is equally skilled with both hands places it on the ordinary left hand. In a more complex case — someone who writes with the right hand but does his other work with the left (or vice versa) — there is a dispute: some say the weaker hand determines it, and some say the writing hand is considered "right," so the tefillin are placed on the hand opposite it. Rabbi Yosef Chaim discusses the view of the Kabbalist Maharai Tzemach, that a left-handed person must never deviate from everyone else's order, his reasoning being grounded in the Kabbalah, and arrives at a practical conclusion: a left-handed person should follow Maran and the straightforward halachic authorities (placing the tefillin on his left hand, which is the "right" for everyone, and praying that way), but after the prayer he should also put on tefillin on the ordinary left hand (without a blessing invoking God's Name and Kingship, only contemplating it in his heart, and reciting the Shema without blessings) — so as to fulfill the mitzvah according to all views; for this he needs two sets of hand-tefillin (one suited to each hand; only one set of head-tefillin is needed), since one set cannot be used for both hands — the knot of the letter yud would come out on the outside if it were turned over. Regarding someone who writes with the ordinary right hand (not left-handed), one may simply rely on the view that the writing hand is considered the right hand, without troubling him to place tefillin twice.
takeaways: A left-handed person (who does his work with his left hand) places the hand-tefillin on his left hand (which is the "right" for everyone); to fulfill the mitzvah according to all views, it is proper (though not obligatory) to also place a second set of tefillin on the other hand without a blessing.
One who writes with the ordinary right hand but does other things with the left may rely on the view that the writing hand determines the placement, without a double placement.

paragraphs: Zeman hannachat tepillin babboqer mishsheyyireh et chabero hirgil immo qetzat berichuq arba ammot veyakkirennu, vetob leacher velo lehaqdim, veim taa vehinnicha tepillin beod layla uberak alehem en tzarik lachazor ulebarek kesheyyair hayyom, vekannizkar b"eliyya raba" seip qatan g' ushear acharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: The time for putting on tefillin in the morning begins from when one can recognize an acquaintance at a distance of four amot. It is good to be careful to delay this time slightly rather than to do it early. One who erred and put on tefillin before dawn, and recited the blessing over them, need not repeat the blessing when daylight comes.
takeaways: The time for tefillin begins when one can recognize an acquaintance at a distance of four amot; it is good to delay slightly rather than do it early.

paragraphs: Lo yachalotz shel yad legamre ad sheyyachalotz shel rosh, deqayma lan kol zeman shebben eneka yihyu shettayim vezeh hu seder chalitzatam, techilla yasir hakkerikot shel haetzba, veyasir gam ken shettayim veshalosh kerikot meal zeroo, kede laasot hachalitza kemo hahannacha shehinnicha et tepillin shel yad techilla remez laddabar kaasher "yachnu ken yissau" (bammidbar b, yz), ak lo yasir et tepillin shel yad legamre mippene shetztzarik leqayyem mah sheamar "uletotapot ben eneka" (shemot yg, tz), shehu rotzeh lomar kol zeman shebben eneka yihyu shettayim, lekak achar shehesir shettayim ushelosha kerikot ditpillin shel yad meal hazzeroa, az yasir et tepillin shel rosh meummad veachar kak yesheb umesir et tepillin shel yad legamre meyushshab vekaasher hinnicho meyushshab, veap al gab dahasarat hakkerikot qodem hasarat tepillin shel rosh velo nitparesha lehedya bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, im kol zeh morenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l hikricha ken kede lehashvot dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l im dibre haggemara, vekatab kimdummeh shekken raa et abiv rabbenu morenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l shekkak noheg ukemo shekkatab behaggahato beshaar hakkavvanot vegam besipro "chemdat yisrael" yeuyyan sham, vaani omer sheyyesh hekreach lazeh middibre rabbenu za"l atzmo beshaar hakkavvanot besop nosach hattepilla dap n" ammud d shekkatab shehaya mori za"l mesir tepillin shel rosh meal rosho veku' veachar kak mesir tepillin shel yad veku' yeuyyan sham: amenam hassebara mechayyebet kepi sodan shel debarim shetztzarik shettihyeh hahasara kemo hahannacha shetztzarik lehasir hakkerikot sheal haetzba meummad, veyesheb veyasir hashshelosha kerikot min kerikot hazzeroa meyushshab kaasher kerakam meyushshab, veachar kak yaamod veyasir tepillin shel rosh meummad, ubeseper "chesed laalapim" siman k"ch ot g' mashma sheyyasir gam hashshalosh hakkerikot shel hazzeroa meummad yeuyyan sham, verabbenu chida" za"l b"tzipporen shamir" katab "yasir kerikot haetzba meummad velo zakar kerikot hazzeroa" ayyen sham, venireh detzarik ledaqdeq lehasir hashshalosh kerikot shel hazzeroa meyushshab kaasher hinnicham meyushshab vekaasher katabnu:

clarification.explanation:
When removing the tefillin, one should not remove the hand-tefillin entirely until first removing the head-tefillin, for we hold that "as long as possible there should be two between your eyes." This is the order of removal: first one removes the windings on the finger, and also two or three windings from the arm — so that the removal parallels the placement (since one puts on the hand-tefillin first), hinting at the verse "as they encamped, so they journeyed." But one does not remove the hand-tefillin entirely, in order to fulfill "and for frontlets between your eyes" — meaning that as long as possible there should be two between one's eyes; therefore after removing two or three windings from the arm, one removes the head-tefillin while standing, and then sits and removes the hand-tefillin entirely while seated, just as he put it on while seated.
Although removing the windings before the head-tefillin is not explicit in the words of the Ari, of blessed memory, our teacher Rav Shmuel Vital, of blessed memory, established this practice in order to reconcile the Ari's words with the Gemara, and wrote that it seemed to him he had seen his father, Rav Chaim Vital, of blessed memory, practice this way (in his gloss on "Sha'ar HaKavanot" and in his book "Chemdat Yisrael"); and the Ben Ish Chai adds that there is compelling proof for this from the Ari's own words in "Sha'ar HaKavanot" (at the end of the text of the prayer), where it is written that the Ari himself would remove the head-tefillin first and afterward the hand-tefillin.
However, reason dictates, according to the mystical secret of these matters, that the removal should parallel the placement: remove the windings of the finger while standing; sit and remove the three windings of the arm while seated (as he wound them while seated); then stand and remove the head-tefillin while standing. From "Chesed LaAlafim" (Siman 28) it appears that one removes the windings of the arm while standing as well, and the Chida, of blessed memory (in "Tziporen Shamir"), wrote to remove the windings of the finger while standing and did not mention the windings of the arm at all; in practice, it appears one should be precise to remove the three windings of the arm while seated, as he put them on.
takeaways: One does not remove the hand-tefillin entirely until removing the head-tefillin ("as long as possible there should be two between your eyes").

The order of removal parallels the placement: the finger windings while standing; sit and remove two or three windings of the arm while seated as one wound them; stand and remove the head-tefillin while standing; then sit and remove the hand-tefillin entirely while seated.

"Chesed LaAlafim" implies the arm windings are also removed while standing, and the Chida did not mention them at all; in practice, it appears one should be precise to remove them while seated, as one put them on.

paragraphs: Nakon lachlotz tepillin shel rosh vehattallit bismolo shehi yad keha leharot deqasheh peridatam ukemo shekkatebu haacharonim za"l, veen lachlotz hattepillin ella ad achar alenu leshabbeach veal ken neqavveh lak, uminhag hachakamim lenashsheq hattepillin bishat hannachatan, ubishat chalitzatan, ubeshaa sheyyannichem tok hakkis, lechibbub mitzva:

clarification.explanation: It is proper to remove the head-tefillin and the tallit with the left hand (the weaker hand), to demonstrate that it is difficult to part from them. One should not remove the tefillin before finishing the prayers "Aleinu LeShabeach" and "Al Ken Nekaveh Lach." It is the custom of the sages to kiss the tefillin when putting them on, when removing them, and when placing them into their bag, out of love for the mitzvah.
takeaways: One should remove the tefillin with the left hand, only after finishing "Aleinu LeShabeach," and it is the custom of the sages to kiss the tefillin when putting them on, removing them, and placing them into the bag.

paragraphs: En lachlotz hattepillin ad sheyyilmod bahem techilla, echad hammarbeh veechad hammamit, ki lo yizkeh haadam liqnot shelosha chelqe nepesh rucha neshama ella im ken lomed bitpillin, ubeyoter im lomed bitpillin derabbenu tam, ukemo shekkatab "machaziq beraka" beshem mahara"m peresh za"l ayyen sham:

clarification.explanation: One should not remove the tefillin before studying at least a little Torah while wearing them — whether much or little — for a person does not merit to acquire the three parts of the soul (nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah) unless he studies Torah while wearing tefillin, and all the more so if he also studies while wearing the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam.
takeaways: One should study a little Torah while still wearing tefillin, before removing them, in order to merit the fullness of soul connected to this mitzvah.

paragraphs: Abal beyom rishon asur lehannicha tepillin, abal beyom sheni chayyab achar hanetz hachamma miyyad, veim met lo met beyom echad veniqbar beyom acher asur lehannicha tepillin beyom qebura, veken asur lehannicha tepillin beyom shemua qeroba amenam im met lo met baregel dematchil limnot shiba achar haregel hare zeh chayyab lehannicha tepillin beyom rishon, venitpashshet hamminhag beir haqqodesh yerushalayim tibbaneh vetikkonen vegam poh ir bagdad lehannicha haabel tepillin derabbenu tam kehoraat rabbenu harasha"sh, udelo kerabbenu chida" za"l shekkatab "sheb veal taaseh adip":

clarification.explanation: On the first day (the day of burial, which is the first day of mourning), a mourner may not put on tefillin, but on the second day he is obligated to put them on immediately after sunrise. If a relative died on one day and was buried on another, it is forbidden to put on tefillin on the day of burial itself, and likewise it is forbidden to put on tefillin on the day one learns of a relative's death ("close news"). But if the relative died during a festival — in which case the counting of the seven days of mourning begins only after the festival — the mourner is obligated to put on tefillin already on the first day of mourning. The custom in Jerusalem and Baghdad was that the mourner does put on the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam (contrary to the Chida's view that it is preferable not to put on tefillin at all — "sitting and not acting is preferable").
takeaways: A mourner does not put on tefillin on the first day of mourning (the day of burial, even if different from the day of death), nor on the day he learns of his relative's death ("close news"); but if the relative died during a festival, he is obligated to put on tefillin already on the first day of mourning.
The accepted custom (contrary to the Chida's view) is that the mourner does put on the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam.

paragraphs: Asur litlot tepillin ben habbattim ben haretzuot, vaapillu bishat hannachatam yesh lehachmir shello leechoz beqesher bilbad veyihyeh habbayit taluy ad shemmannicho berosho, ella yiqqach beyado haqqesher im habbayit beyachad veyannicha habbayit bimqomo veachar kak haqqesher bimqomo:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to hold the tefillin suspended in the air by the strap alone — neither the boxes nor the straps. Even at the time of putting them on, one should be stringent not to hold only the knot while the box hangs suspended, but rather to hold the knot together with the box in his hand, place the box in its place, and only afterward secure the knot in its place.
takeaways: One must not put on the tefillin in a manner where the box hangs suspended, supported only by the strap; one should place them together — the box first, then secure the knot.

paragraphs: Keshemmannicha hattepillin betok hakkis shellahem, o keshekkorek hachut shebbepi hakkis lo yiglol hakkis shebbo hattepillin sebib hachut, ella yiglol hachut sebib hakkis vekannizkar baacharonim veyesh medaqdeqin gam bakkis hachitzon shebbo munnach hattallit gadol vekis hattepillin, gam yizzaher bekis hachitzon shebbo munnach hattallit gadol vekis hattepillin shello yannicha hattallit gadol vehassiddur lemala min hattepillin, ella yannicha hattepillin min hatztzad gam yizzaher beheka ditpillin shel rosh utepillin shel yad shenehem munnachim bekis echad lemashmesh bahem beodam betok hakkis kede sheyyeda et tepillin shel yad lehotzio techilla, velo yiteh lehotzi tepillin shel rosh techilla, veim hu lobesh rashi"y verabbenu tam beyachad deaz mukrach sheyyaaseh kis litpillin shel yad vekis litpillin shel rosh yizzaher laasot lahem siman bekisim kede sheyyotzi shel tepillin shel yad techilla:

clarification.explanation: When placing the tefillin into their bag and winding the cord at the bag's opening, one should wind the cord around the bag, not the bag around the cord. Some are also careful regarding the outer bag in which the large tallit and the tefillin bag are kept, not to place the tallit and the prayer book above the tefillin, but rather to place the tefillin to the side. One must also be careful, when the head-tefillin and hand-tefillin are kept together in one bag, to feel for them while still inside the bag, in order to identify the hand-tefillin (so as to take it out first, not mistakenly taking out the head-tefillin first). One who wears both Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin, and must therefore use two separate bags, should make a distinguishing mark on the bags to know to take out the hand-tefillin first.
takeaways: One should wind the cord around the bag (not the reverse), and identify the hand-tefillin by feel before removing it from the bag, so as to take it out first.

paragraphs: Mi shemminhago lilbosh rashi"y verabbenu tam beyachad, vehu korekan yachad lehannicham bakkis yizzaher shello yasim haqqetzitza al meabbarta shel hashsheni ella yannicha haqqetzitzot kullam al haretzuot zeh etzel zeh:

clarification.explanation: One who customarily wears both Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin together, and winds them together before placing them in the bag, must be careful not to place the box of one pair on the "ma'avarta" (the strap-loop passing through the box) of the other pair, but rather to place all the boxes side by side on the straps.
takeaways: When winding two pairs of tefillin (Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam) together, the boxes should be placed side by side, not one on top of the other's ma'avarta.

paragraphs: Tzarik lehizzaher shello yapicha bahem umi sheyyesh lo mechosh shemmesabbeb lo hapacha yannicha tepillin biqriat shema ubirkoteha utepillat haamida bilbad, veyishtaddel lehaamid atzmo bizman muat zeh shello yapicha vekannizkar baacharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: One must be careful not to pass gas while wearing tefillin. One who suffers from an ailment that causes a tendency to pass gas should limit himself to wearing tefillin only during the reading of the Shema and its blessings and the Amidah prayer, making an effort to restrain himself during this brief period.
takeaways: One prone to passing gas may limit himself to wearing tefillin only during the Shema and the Amidah prayer, making an effort to restrain himself during that short time.

paragraphs: Lo yassicha dato mehattepillin, veraq bishat eseq hattora usheat tepillat haamida patur, veyesh mitchakkemim liktob begilyon hassiddur bekol dap lemala umin hatztzad otiyyot "tepillin" gedolot lihyot lahem siyyua lehessach haddaat, veellu en tzerikin liktob betok hassiddur atzmo ella yiktebu al neyar bipne atzmo berosh ubatztzedadin, veyihyeh middat hanneyar gadol meat middap hassiddur beopen sheim yannicha hanneyar betok hassiddur ben haddappim yihyu nirin leenayv tebot "tepillin" vetihyeh lo lemazkeret:

clarification.explanation: One should not let his mind wander from the tefillin while wearing them, except during Torah study or the Amidah prayer, when he is exempt from this concern. Some employ a device: writing the word "tefillin" in large letters at the top and side of every page of the prayer book, as a reminder not to let their mind wander. It is preferable to write this not within the prayer book itself, but on a separate sheet, slightly larger than the pages of the prayer book, so that when placed between the pages, the word "tefillin" stands out to the eye and serves as a reminder.
takeaways: One's mind should not wander from the tefillin (except during Torah study and the Amidah prayer); it is recommended to use a separate reminder sheet (not written within the prayer book itself) bearing the word "tefillin" in large letters.

paragraphs: Mi shennapelu lo tepelayv miyyado, nakon sheyyitanneh yom echad beoto hayyom, veim i epshar lo lehitannot yipdeh hattaanit bitzdaqa, veim napelu bihyotam tok kisam en tzarik lehitannot ella day latet peruta achat litzdaqa ubesipre haq' "rab pealim" katabti besiyyata dishmayya bitshuba daapillu im napelu begobah pachot measara tepachim yitanneh yom echad, velo kemo shechoshebim haolam debaenan gobah asara tepachim:

clarification.explanation: One whose tefillin fell from his hand (while exposed, not inside their bag) — it is proper for him to fast one day on that same day; and if he cannot fast, he should redeem the fast with charity. If they fell while still inside their bag, there is no need to fast, and it suffices to give one perutah to charity. Rabbi Yosef Chaim adds a novel ruling: even if they fell from a height lower than ten tefachim (contrary to the common assumption that only a fall from ten tefachim or more requires a fast), one should still fast one day.
takeaways: An exposed fall of the tefillin from the hand (even from a low height) requires a day's fast or redemption with charity; a fall while inside the bag requires only a perutah to charity.

paragraphs: Keshecholetz tepelayv tob shehu beatzmo yeqappelem veyannichem bekis lechibbub mitzva, velo keotam shennotenim hattepillin lashshammash shellahem leqappelo, vedugma lezeh matzinu deameru rabbotenu za"l gabbe seper tora haggolel notel sakar keneged kullan, gam yizzaher leqappelo ulehannicho bakkis tekep umiyyad achar sheyyachalotz oto, velo keotam shecholetzim umannichim oto mitztzedam, veachar ezeh regaim meqappelim oto, ki en zeh kabod lattepillin sheyyehe munnach kak, ubizman sheyyesh lo hekreach lekak kegon shecholetzan qodem tepillat musap berosh chodesh deeno yakol leqappelo tekep mippene sherotzeh lehitpallel musap im hatztzibbur, yizzaher shello yannicha haqqetzitza behippuk dehaynu tzad hammabarta lemala vegupo shel bayit lematta, ella yannichennu beyosher vetekep yiqpelu achar tepillat musap:

clarification.explanation: When removing the tefillin, it is proper for the person himself to fold them and place them in the bag, out of love for the mitzvah, rather than handing them to his attendant to fold — similar to what our sages said regarding one who rolls a Torah scroll, that he receives a reward equal to all the others. One should be careful to fold and put them into the bag immediately after removal, not leaving the tefillin set aside for a while before folding, since it is not respectful to the tefillin to be left lying that way. In a case where there is a compelling need to delay (such as removing them before the Musaf prayer on Rosh Chodesh, when one wishes to pray with the congregation and cannot fold immediately), one should be careful at least not to leave the box upside down (with the ma'avarta-side facing up), but rather to place it upright, and to fold it immediately after the Musaf prayer.
takeaways: It is preferable that the person himself fold and place his tefillin in the bag immediately after removing them, rather than leaving them set aside or handing them to someone else.
